question.text: In the 20th century, this Southern Hemisphere country built a nearly 3500-mile fence to keep dingos, a type of wild dog that lives in this country's outback, out of its more populated southeast.
question.clue: Governor William Bligh was deposed in the Rum Rebellion in this country.

swap.text: The "history wars" began after the Bringing Them Home report was released on these people. This term refers to Australian Aborigines taken from their families as children by the Australian government.
swap.clue: An official 2007 apology to these people and their descendants was made by then-Prime Minister Kevin Rudd.

question.leadin: This colony was founded by the First Fleet on January 26, 1788, and its first governor was Arthur Phillip.
question.text: Name this colony which originated around Port Jackson. Lachlan Macquarie was the final governor of this territory.
question.clue: The Tenterfield Oration, calling for states to unify for purposes of defense, was given in this state, which was also the landing spot for Arthur Phillip and the First Fleet.

swap.leadin: Descendents of convicts known as "currency lads" carried out raids on feral horses called brumbies in the bush and this region.
swap.text: Name this region where jackaroos established "cattle empires" around stations. The disastrous Emu War occurred in this rural region of central Australia.
swap.clue: An overland telegraph line through this region was scouted by Robert Burke and William Wills but was eventually built through Alice Springs.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the failure of the Gallipoli Campaign.
question.text: The date of the Gallipoli landing is a day of remembrance for this expeditionary force, which was composed of soldiers from two British commonwealths.
question.answerHtml: ANZAC [or the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps]
question.clue: Their most notable action is remembered in the song titled "And the Band Played" a certain nationalist folk tune, was supported by the French from Kum Kale, and was advocated by Winston Churchill.

swap.leadin: Australia has struggled with the civil rights of these people.
swap.text: These indigenous Australians were frequently massacred at the beginning of British colonization of Australia.
swap.clue: Many of these people were taken from their families and integrated into white culture, becoming the Stolen Generation.

question.leadin: As Treasurer of Australia, this man oversaw the creation of the Australian Dollar and later ended the pegging of the currency to the British pound.
question.text: Name this Prime Minister who more famously went missing while swimming at Cheviot Beach in 1967. Ironically, a swimming pool in Melbourne was named in his honor.
question.clue: This prime minister declared that he was "all the way with LBJ" in showing his country's support for the Vietnam War.

swap.text: On this island, British colonists tried to corral natives using a giant island-wide human chain, but only were able to capture two people. That failed campaign was part of the Black War on this island.
swap.clue: In 1996, Martin Bryant killed 35 people on this island.

question.text: The band Midnight Oil wore jackets with "SORRY" on the back to draw attention to the Stolen Generations during the 2000 Summer Olympics in this Australian city. This is the most populous city in Australia.
question.clue: Lachlan Macquarie ("LACK-lan muh-KWAIR-ee") was placed in charge of this city after John Macarthur overthrew governor William Bligh in the Rum Rebellion.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about modern gun control measures around the world.
swap.text: Australian Prime Minister John Howard implemented a gun buyback program and severely restricted private gun ownership following this 1996 mass shooting in Tasmania.
swap.clue: This November 1894 event carried out by General Yamaji Motoharu's forces, which killed somewhere between 1,000 and 20,000 people.

question.text: This bushranger belonged to the Greta mob and a later "gang" named after him. While under siege by the police at Glenrowan, this man wore an iron bulletproof suit.
question.clue: This man sent a lewd note wrapped around calves' testicles to Jeremiah McCormack's wife.

swap.text: In 2017, Australian Aboriginals and Torres Strait Islanders held a convention at this rock formation in central Australia that is sacred to local tribes.
swap.clue: A major event in the Aboriginal Rights Movement was the 1985 ceremony that returned ownership of this monolith to the Anangu. A 99-year lease on this enormous monolith has kept the Anangu from forbidding people to climb it.

question.leadin: A leader of this party named Johannes Strydom was nicknamed "Lion of the North."
question.text: Identify this party, which first won a majority in parliament in a 1948 election under Daniel Francois Malan's leadership. Its government implemented the Group Areas Act and the Land Acts.
question.clue: This defunct right-wing party first led by J. B. M. Hertzog, who formed a government after defeating the United Party led by Jan Smuts in 1924.

swap.leadin: This party took office under Malcolm Fraser after governor-general John Kerr controversially ousted Gough ("goff") Whitlam in 1975.
swap.text: Name this party, which made extensive spending cuts after succeeding the Keating government. During the 1970s, this party began a coalition arrangement with the National Country Party.
swap.answerHtml: Liberal Party of Australia [or LPA; accept word forms like Australian Liberal Party or Australians Liberals; prompt on Liberal Party and ask “of what country”; don’t accept ALP]
swap.clue: This party regained power after the Loans Affair presaged ("PRESS-idged") the collapse of Gough Whitlam's ("goff WIT-lum's") government.

question.text: A landmark 1891 sheep shearers' strike led to the founding of this party under the "Tree of Knowledge." This party's later leaders included Billy Hughes and Gough Whitlam.
question.answerHtml: Australian Labor Party [or ALP; prompt on Labor Party with “of what country?”]
question.clue: This political party passed important social reforms under leaders like Bob Hawke and Gough Whitlam.

swap.text: Menzies built credit among the middle class by calling them by this name, which titles a notable 1942 speech he made emphasizing his connections to ordinary people.

question.text: Later, New Zealand and Australia laid out their post-WWII military and political goals in the Canberra Pact, signed by this Australian prime minister. Frank Forde finished this prime minister's term after his death in office.
question.clue: This prime minister of Australia during World War Two, a member of the Labour Party, defended the policy by declaring the country "the home of the British race" in a 1942 speech.

swap.text: This Australian Labor Party PM's foreign minister Gareth Evans claimed the Santa Cruz massacre was merely an "aberration." This personal friend of Suharto served as PM from 1991 to '96.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the history of convict-era Australia.
question.text: The Australian-born children of emancipated convicts were known by this term, contrasted with "sterling" or English-born settlers.
question.clue: Edible examples of these items include Mongolian tea bricks, and, in Rome, salt.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about gold rushes in Australia and New Zealand during the mid-1800s.
swap.text: This man led the gold miners at the Battle of the Eureka Stockade and parlayed his subsequent fame into a long political career, rising all the way to Speaker of the Victorian Legislative Assembly.
